{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABXX1cgg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhA77LQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 7, "title": "Upgrade Three.js to the latest stable release across the emulator", "body": "## Problem

The WebXR emulator extension still uses **Three.js r111** (`three: "0.111.0"` in `package.json`), with legacy vendored Three.js, loaders, and controls under `src/app/three/`. Its DevTools panel and emulated AR scene use APIs and shader code tied to that old release. This creates maintenance/compatibility risk, and earlier dependency validation reported a high-severity advisory affecting the retained legacy Three.js.

The latest published stable Three.js release checked when opening this Issue is **r186** (published 2026-09-24). A dependency-version-only change would leave mismatched runtime copies and removed/changed APIs.

## Expected outcome

Upgrade the entire extension's Three.js usage from r111 to **the latest stable official Three.js release available at implementation time** (r186 as of 2026-10-15), including its DevTools panel, AR renderer, GLTF/OBJ loaders, OrbitControls/TransformControls, and any affected shader/rendering code. Deliver a working, cohesive update in a PR against `dev`, not a package bump with broken legacy vendor scripts.

Preserve the existing TypeScript and Manifest V3 architecture and supported VR/AR emulation. Do not use prereleases or downgrade to an intermediate version as the final result. Incremental upgrades *during development* to diagnose breaking changes are fine, provided the submitted result uses the latest stable release.

## Context

- Follow the repository [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), and PR template. Work from and target `dev`; use English in collaboration artifacts.
- `package.json` currently pins `three` to `0.111.0`, while `src/app/panel.html` loads vendored `three.js`, `GLTFLoader.js`, `OBJLoader.js`, `OrbitControls.js`, and `TransformControls.js` from `src/app/three/`. `src/app/panel.ts` uses the legacy `window.THREE` global. The AR renderer in `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts` imports npm Three.js and `three/examples/jsm/`.
- The current custom AR screen material modifies shader source with `onBeforeCompile`; check its texture sampling/color-space behavior against the new renderer/shader chunks. Old geometry constructors such as `BoxBufferGeometry` and `PlaneBufferGeometry` and old controls/loaders should be migrated to supported APIs. Inspect the complete codebase for other breaking changes.
- Make the panel use matching modern Three.js and addon modules, preferably bundled locally with the existing TypeScript/Rollup build rather than mixing incompatible vendor globals with the new npm dependency. Update `build.ts`, HTML references, type declarations, and any tests that rely on `window.THREE` or legacy addon internals. Keep all extension code packaged locally (no CDN, remote script injection, or unsafe eval).
- Preserve Manifest V3 MAIN-world synchronous WebXR polyfill injection and its isolation from privileged content scripts, service-worker messaging/recovery, as well as the separately packaged Firefox build.
- Official references: [Three.js releases](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/releases), [Three.js migration guide](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/wiki/Migration-Guide), [Three.js docs](https://threejs.org/docs/).

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Confirm the newest stable Three.js release at implementation time, document the selected exact release, upgrade `three` to it, and update/reproduce `package-lock.json` with `npm ci`. Do not leave an old `three` version used at runtime.
- [ ] Replace/remove the legacy `src/app/three/` runtime copies, or explicitly document any non-Three.js assets that must remain. Ensure panel and AR code use compatible Three.js core and addons of **the same updated release**, without mixing r111 globals and modern modules.
- [ ] Update `src/app/panel.ts`, `src/app/panel.html`, `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts`, `src/polyfill/MyControls.ts`, and other affected files to supported modern APIs. Cover loader results, model loading, Orbit/TransformControls behavior, raycasting, geometry, materials, render targets, texture/color-space handling, and WebGL2 requirements.
- [ ] Restore the AR screen's combined texture rendering/shader logic for the new renderer, with correct colors/orientation/visibility and no compile/runtime WebGL errors. Keep the packaged `assets/hall_empty.glb`, headset OBJ, and controller GLB loading correctly.
- [ ] Update TypeScript declarations, `build.ts`, browser bundles, HTML references, and tests (including any DevTools 3D scene/camera probe depending on legacy Three.js internals). Preserve the MV3 packaging/security and synchronous WebXR injection behavior. No runtime fetches of third-party JavaScript.
- [ ] Keep existing device selection/stereo settings/persistence, DevTools model and controller visualization, headset/controller transforms and gizmos, select/squeeze input, session exit, AR virtual room/tablet/touch, persistent and transient AR hit testing, and worker restart/frame-routing behavior working. Any unavoidable visible rendering changes should be explained.
- [ ] Run and record the actual results of `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, and `npm run test:browser` against a current desktop Chrome/Chromium release. Fix migration-introduced failures; distinguish pre-existing limitations and optional checks from passing checks.
- [ ] Verify the 3D panel and AR room using browser-rendered screenshots or equivalent visual inspection in addition to functional assertions, especially loaders, transform gizmos, raycast intersections, and texture/shader output. Record browser version, reproduction procedure, and results; no physical XR hardware is required unless a concrete issue necessitates it.
- [ ] Run dependency security checks as applicable and document whether the old Three.js advisory is resolved; report remaining unrelated advisories without claiming they are fixed.
- [ ] Update README/developer notes to describe the selected Three.js version, removed vendor scripts/new bundling, build/runtime requirements, and any meaningful migration limitations. Submit an implementation PR against `dev` and request review following repo guidance.

## Optional validation

- Run Firefox MV3 runtime/DevTools VR/AR regression tests in a supported Firefox version, if available; the Firefox package must at least build before merge.
- Compare before/after screenshots under the same XR scene, camera poses, and device settings, and test representative external WebXR sample apps.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Build, package, compatibility and browser rendering checks should be completed before merge. Browser-store publication is out of scope.
